question: What is the meaning of dimensions in relation to physical properties, technical properties?
description: Dimensions refer to the size and shape of an object, which are essential for understanding its physical properties and technical properties. For example, in the context of sustainable construction, dimensions are crucial for determining the structural integrity and energy efficiency of a building. They also play a key role in the design and manufacturing of products, ensuring that they meet specific requirements and standards. In the provided context, dimensions are included in the overview of physical properties, highlighting their importance in understanding the characteristics of materials and products.

3.1.3
Composition properties
Figure 5 shows the composition property facet. This block of ontology helps to optimise
the selection, processing, and assembly of the constituent parts and materials of a product
and facilitates their separation, dismantling, and recycling at the end of life of a product
to maximise the circularity.
Figure 5: Composition property facet of the MPO.
CompositionProperty has two subclasses, ConstituentPart and ConstituentMaterial. For
example, crossbeam has constituent materials carbon fibre, glass fibre, epoxy resin, alu-
minium, foam, and film adhesive that have mass, and a source and destination in a circular
economy.
